title: The Passion Week
description: The last week of Jesus' life, day by day: the crowds of Palm Sunday, the temple overturned, the trick questions, the woman with the alabaster box, the upper room, Gethsemane, the arrest, the trials, the cross, the silent Saturday and the empty tomb. From the King James Bible, told slowly, with a prayer to close.

beats.say: A third of the gospels is about one week. Matthew, Mark, Luke and John slow down, almost hour by hour, as Jesus walks toward Jerusalem and the cross.
Luke says that when the time was come, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem. He knew exactly what was waiting there. He went anyway.
Let us walk through that week together, day by day, from the shouts of Hosanna to the silence of the tomb, and on to the morning everything changed.
He sent two disciples for a donkey's colt, fulfilling an old prophecy: thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass. Kings rode warhorses. This one rode a donkey.
A very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way. Passover pilgrims, filling the road into the city.
Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest. Hosanna means: save us now.
And all the city was moved, saying, Who is this? The question of the whole week. By Friday, the same city would give a very different answer.
When he came near, he beheld the city, and wept over it: If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! The King cried on his own parade.
The next day he went into the temple and found a marketplace: animals for sacrifice, moneychangers charging pilgrims to swap their coins, all in the only court where foreigners could pray.

Jesus cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers: It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
Then the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them. He cleared out the trade, and made room for the people the trade had kept out.
And the children were crying in the temple, Hosanna to the Son of David. The priests were furious. Jesus quoted a psalm: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise.
What has crowded out prayer in the temple of your own life? He still comes to overturn tables, not to condemn you, but to make room for you to meet God again.
All day Tuesday his enemies came at him with trap questions, hoping to turn the crowd or the Romans against him. Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?
Shew me the tribute money. Whose is this image? They said, Caesar's. Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.
The coin bore Caesar's image, so give it to Caesar. And you bear God's image, so give yourself to God. They marvelled, and left him, and went their way.
A lawyer asked which was the great commandment. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.
And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets. Every rule in scripture is love, spelled out.
In Bethany, at supper in the house of Simon the leper, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
Some had indignation: Why was this waste of the ointment made? For it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and have been given to the poor.
Let her alone. She hath done what she could: she is come aforehand to anoint my body to the burying. She understood, before anyone else did, that he was going to die.
Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her. And it still is, tonight.
That same night Judas went to the chief priests to betray him. And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. One gave everything. One sold everything.
In a large upper room, before the feast of the passover, Jesus knew that his hour was come. Having loved his own which were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
He laid aside his garments, took a towel, poured water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples' feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.
And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
Then they sang an hymn, and went out into the mount of Olives. Jesus sang, knowing what was waiting in the dark beyond the city wall.
They came to a garden called Gethsemane, which means oil press. Sit ye here, while I shall pray. He took Peter, James and John a little further.
My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death: tarry ye here, and watch. And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless not what I will, but what thou wilt.
Three times he came back and found them sleeping. Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour? The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
He prayed alone while his friends slept. Whatever you are facing that no one else can carry with you, he has knelt in that place first.
While he yet spake, cometh Judas, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves. He had given them a sign: Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he.
Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss? Even then, Jesus called him friend.
Peter drew a sword and cut off a servant's ear. Jesus touched his ear, and healed him. The last miracle before the cross was for one of the men who came to arrest him.
And they all forsook him, and fled. Every one of them. He walked into the night alone, so that no one who trusts him ever has to.
Through the night they tried him before the high priest. False witnesses contradicted each other. Jesus held his peace, and answered nothing.
Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed? And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power. The high priest tore his clothes. Guilty of blasphemy.
At dawn they took him to Pilate. The governor found no fault in him, and offered the crowd a choice: Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews? They cried out: Crucify him.
Pilate took water, and washed his hands before the multitude: I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it. Water cannot wash away a choice.
So Pilate released Barabbas, a murderer, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified. The guilty man walked free, and the innocent took his place. That is the gospel, in one scene.
The soldiers clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head, and mocked him: Hail, King of the Jews. They meant it as a joke. It was true.
And it was the third hour, and they crucified him. And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
The passers by and the priests mocked: He saved others; himself he cannot save. They were right. He could not save himself and save us too. He chose us.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost. And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom. The way to God, torn open from above.
And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
Joseph of Arimathaea, a secret disciple, went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body. He took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulchre that was hewn in stone.
A great stone was rolled across the door. The women watched where he was laid. And they rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.
The gospels say almost nothing about Saturday. It was the longest silence in history. If you are living in a Saturday tonight, when God seems quiet and hope is buried, remember: Sunday is coming.
Very early in the morning, the women came to the sepulchre with spices, and found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre. And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
Two men stood by them in shining garments: Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen.
The week that began with Hosanna, save us now, ended with the answer. He did. The cross was not the end of the story. It was the way through.
Let us pray. Lord Jesus, you set your face toward Jerusalem for me. Thank you for walking all the way to the cross, when you could have turned back on any day of that week.
Come into my life the way you came into the temple. Overturn what crowds out prayer, and heal what is broken. Teach me to love God with everything, and my neighbour as myself.
When I sleep while others suffer, wake me. When I run away, find me. When I live in a Saturday silence, hold me until Sunday comes.
Like the thief beside you, I ask: Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. You are risen, as you said. Hosanna. Save us now. Amen.
